analysis: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) commonly used in the treatment of estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Its known adverse effects include an increased risk of thromboembolism and endometrial carcinoma, both of which are well-documented in clinical literature. The risk of developing carcinoma in the contralateral breast is also recognized, although it is less frequently emphasized compared to the other two risks. Cataracts have been reported in some studies, but the association is not as strong or as commonly acknowledged as the other adverse effects. Given this context, cataracts are the least commonly linked adverse effect of tamoxifen use, making it the most appropriate answer to the question of which adverse effect is not typically associated with its use.
